about.what: Shared vectors for DX4's widened `subagents` body ({subagents, jobs, mcp}) and its `output` answer, as the desk composite (MAWS docs/doperpowers/specs/2026-10-15-desk-design.md, DX4 'Jobs and agent status', 'Precedence', '`output`') defines them. Both producers derive them from transcript rows: the plane (doperpowers skills/sminos/scripts/sminos_jobs.py, pinned by tests/sminos/jobs_parity.py) and DC9's fake machine, which vendors this file. Written by tests/sminos/dx4-jobs.gen.py; every expected body is written by hand from the rules below, never computed by either implementation.
inputs: `cases[*].input.session`: {id, running}; `running` false when the session's process is gone (presence's record null).
`input.main`: the loop's transcript rows in file order (the main loop's for a main-scope subscription).
`input.metas`: [{agentId, meta}], each meta a subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json verbatim, in the plane's order; one `subagents` entry per meta, in this order.

`input.agentFiles`: {agentId: {rows, size, mtimeMs} | null} for subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl: its rows in file order, its size in bytes and mtime in ms (inputs, no clock); null or absent: the file is gone or unreadable. A nested agent's outcome is read from its parent's file (parentAgentId).

`input.bridge`: the bridge's agent state, {agents: [{agentId, parentAgentId, subagentType, description, name?, background?, model?, toolUseId?, agentType?, running}]} (the child's snapshot `agents` with every `agent` event applied), or null for no bridge.
derived: `file`: {size, mtimeMs} as given; `firstAt`/`lastAt` the `timestamp` of the first and of the last row of the agent's file that carries a string timestamp (null when none). Absent when the file is.
Everything else in `expect` follows from the rules.
rules: Rows read: an assistant row's tool_use blocks named Agent or Task, Bash, Monitor, TaskStop (by id; input.description, input.command, input.task_id, and an Agent or Task call's input.run_in_background); the user row's tool_result for those ids (is_error) with its toolUseResult; a task-notification, in either of the two forms the engine writes (both read alike, elements <task-id>, <tool-use-id>, <output-file>, <status>, <summary>, <event>, each trimmed): an attachment `queued_command` with commandMode `task-notification` (its `prompt`), or a plain row of type `user` whose `origin.kind` is `task-notification` and whose message content (a string, or its text blocks joined) starts with `<task-notification>`, or with the engine's preamble `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]\n` (written before it in a subagent's transcript) then, from the first blank line followed by `<task-notification>`, that notification; one notification per row. A row without that origin is no notification whatever its text (a person can type it); an attachment `task_status` {taskId, taskType, description, status, deltaSummary, outputFilePath}; an attachment `mcp_instructions_delta` {addedNames, removedNames}. Each row's `timestamp` is its `at`.

Evidence words (`raw`): a notification's <status> (one with no <status> is no evidence, but for the expiry rule below); a task_status's `status`; an Agent result row: `async_launched` when it is a launch (the launch rule below), else `error` when is_error, else toolUseResult.status when a string, else `completed`; a TaskStop call naming the task whose result is not is_error: `stopped`. The table maps a word to {status, terminal}; the launch rule and the expiry rule below map their own; any other word is unrecognized.

The launch rule, beside the table (not a row of it): an Agent result row that is a launch is a background agent's start, non-terminal running evidence from the rows: {status `running`, raw `async_launched`}, at precedence (3), below every terminal word and below known process death. A result row is a launch when its toolUseResult.status is `async_launched`, or, when the row has no toolUseResult and is not is_error, when its text (a string, or its text blocks joined) is one of the engine's launch texts, matched exactly: it starts with `Async agent launched successfully.`, then optionally a space and a parenthesis closed on that line, then a line break and `agentId: ` (2.1.2xx-2.1.300, toolUseResult or not: some are written without one); or it is exactly `Fork started — processing in background` (a fork's launch, written without a toolUseResult). Any other text, the launch line quoted after other text, or the first line alone without the `agentId: ` line that follows it, is no launch. A row with a toolUseResult is decided by it, whatever its text: an agent's own answer may begin as a launch does.

The expiry rule, beside the table (not a row of it): a task-notification with no <status> for a task the loop holds as a monitor (a Monitor result started it), whose <event> begins `[Monitor expired after ` or `[Monitor timed out` (the engine's expiry lines, 2.1.300), is terminal: {status `completed`, raw `expired`, summary the <event> text}. Any other notification with no <status> (a monitor's event, an agent resumed by the user) stays no evidence, and so does an expiry line for a task that is not a monitor.

An agent's evidence: the rows of its loop (the main loop's for an agent without parentAgentId; its parent's file for a nested one) that name it: the result row for its toolUseId (meta.toolUseId, else spawn.toolUseId), a notification whose <task-id> is the agentId or whose <tool-use-id> is that toolUseId, a task_status whose taskId is the agentId, a non-error TaskStop whose task_id is the agentId. For a background agent (meta.requestShape `background`, spawn.background true, or its call's input.run_in_background true or the string "true", as the engine writes either) a result row whose word is not async_launched does not count. None of these is needed to know a launch: many metas have no requestShape, a bridge seeded from $.agent.list() has no background, and many calls of agents that run in the background carry no run_in_background.

`outcome` folds the agent's evidence in row order: a recognized word replaces the outcome ({status, raw, at, summary?, outputFile?} from that row) unless the outcome is terminal and the word is not; an unrecognized word replaces only `raw` of an existing outcome (and is dropped when there is none). `summary`: a notification's <summary> (an expiry notice's <event>), a task_status's deltaSummary, a TaskStop result's toolUseResult.message; `outputFile`: a notification's <output-file>, a task_status's outputFilePath, a launch's toolUseResult.outputFile; each present only when the deciding row carries it.

`status` and `evidence`, the first that holds: (1) the outcome is terminal: its status, `rows`; (2) the session's process is gone: `exited`, `session`; the parent (meta.parentAgentId, else spawn.parentAgentId) has a status completed, failed, stopped or exited: `exited`, `parent`; the bridge holds the agent with running false: `exited`, `bridge`; (3) the bridge holds it with running true: `running`, `bridge`; the outcome's status is running: `running`, `rows`; (4) `unknown`, `none`. The bridge counts only while the session's process runs.

`running`: the bridge's, present while the bridge holds the agent and the session's process runs. `spawn`: the bridge's entry's spawn fields among {parentAgentId, subagentType, description, name, background, model, toolUseId} that it has, present when the bridge holds the agent (kept after the process is gone).

`jobs`: one per Bash result whose toolUseResult.backgroundTaskId is set (kind `shell`) and per Monitor result whose toolUseResult.taskId is set (kind `monitor`), in the order of those result rows: taskId, toolUseId, `startedAt` the call row's at, `description` the call's input.description ("" when none), `command` the call's input.command when present, `outputFile` the latest path any row named for the task (null until one does), and the status of the fold above over the rows naming the task (notification by <task-id>, task_status by taskId, non-error TaskStop by task_id), starting from running: terminal: that status with `endedAt` its row's at; else `exited` when the session's process is gone; else `running`. `summary` the deciding row's, when it has one.
`mcp`: names from each mcp_instructions_delta in row order, its removedNames first: each removed name dropped, then each added name appended unless present; [{name}].

Paths for `output`: the latest path a row named for each task id: a task_status's outputFilePath, a notification's <output-file>, a Bash result's text after 'Output is being written to: ' up to whitespace, a trailing '.' dropped.
output: `outputCases[*].input`: `session`; `roots`, the canonical roots the caller derives (DX4's set: one per slug, each <resolved tmp>/claude-<uid>/<slug>/<session>/tasks/); `main`, the loop's rows; `layout`, entries to make in order under a temporary directory: {path, file: text (UTF-8)} | {path, symlink: target} | {path, dir: true}, parents made as needed; `request` {taskId, tail}.
Materialize: replace `<ROOT>` in every string of the case (rows, roots, layout, expect) with the realpath of a fresh temporary directory, then make the layout.

Answer: a task id no row names (no job, notification or task_status for it): unknown-task. No path named: missing, path null. The named path must end in the whole components <session>/tasks/<taskId>.output, and its realpath must be exactly <realpath of a root>/<taskId>.output (under a root in whole components, and the task's own file, not another's) and a regular file once opened; otherwise refused. A path that passes with nothing there: missing with the path. Else ok: size the file's bytes, the last `tail` bytes read from the end; when that window does not start the file, the text starts after the first line break inside it (no cut when it has none); decoded UTF-8 with replacement; `from` the byte offset the text starts at; `truncated` from > 0.
`reason` (refused) is a sentence for the human: compared only as a non-empty string; every other field exactly.

cases.name: launches written without a toolUseResult, in a cold open of the ended session
cases.why: No bridge, the session over, every meta of the older form (no requestShape). A launch result with no toolUseResult is still the launch when its text is the engine's: a ran with run_in_background "true" (a string, as the engine also writes it), b's call carries no run_in_background, f is a fork (its launch text is the fork's). Each is exited (session) with the launch as its outcome; read as `completed`, they would be completed (rows) here while the live session, its bridge knowing them as background, said exited. g's and h's calls ran in the background (run_in_background true, and "true") and their results are in a wording no rule knows: they do not count, so g and h have no outcome. x1 quotes the launch text after its own, and x2 starts as the launch does but names no agent: both are a foreground agent's answer, completed.
